subject: Streamline AI p95 spike — tradeoffs, mitigation, and customer note
messages:
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, sara@streamline.ai
Cc: 
Date: 2028-06-28T09:12:34-07:00
Subject: Streamline AI p95 spike — immediate tradeoffs + customer note

Team —

We’re seeing a sustained p95 jump for Streamline’s gen-api traffic starting ~09:00 PT. Quick snapshot: baseline p95 ~180ms, current p95 ~820ms, request rate stable (no QPS surge). Error rates are unchanged. Latency increase is concentrated on long prompts (median tokens > 800).

What we’ve observed so far:
- KV cache hit ratio dropped ~22% for Streamline keys (see perf-graphs-0628.png).
- A small subset of requests are hitting an attention-kernel tail path that’s 3–4x slower for long sequences.
- Autoscaler has not triggered additional capacity (traffic distribution per shard is uneven).

Immediate asks:
1) Karthik — can eng flip the short-term mitigations (raise batching timeout to 50ms + disable streaming on this route) to reduce overhead? What’s the risk to tail latency vs increased queuing?
2) Marissa — product needs a crisp tradeoff: enable int8 quantized variant (lower memory/latency, potential small quality delta) vs prioritize KV-warmup and routing fixes. Which should we push as recommended mitigation to the customer?
3) Jordan/CS — I drafted a short customer note (attached) asking for temporary throttling of extremely long prompts; I want to share with Streamline after we align.

Attachments: perf-graphs-0628.png, canary-config.diff, cust-brief-streamline-0628-draft.pdf

I’ll start a canary with an increased batch window on a single shard in 10 minutes and watch impact. Please reply in-thread — need sign-off in next 30m so we can message Sara with an ETA.

Thanks,
Olga
SRE Lead — Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-28T09:25:12-07:00
Subject: Re: Streamline AI p95 spike — immediate tradeoffs + customer note

Ack — good color. Quick notes from infra side: we can implement two tactics immediately (non-disruptive to model weights):

Option A (fast, reversible):
- Increase continuous-batching window to 50ms for Streamline route only. Expected effect: reduce per-token kernel invocation overhead for long requests, may add queuing latency for short requests (low QPS on shorts right now).
- Force-perform kv-prefetch for the top 10 keys in the canary shard to mitigate cold-kv hits.
Estimated time to roll: ~12 minutes for canary; full rollout 30–45m if we see p95 drop ~30%

Option B (medium risk):
- Switch to int8 quantized variant of the serving model for this customer. Latency improvement: 20–35% on p95 in our bench; quality regression improbable but we need a small eval. Deploy time: ~40–60m (model variant routing + quick canary).

Option C (longer): routing redistribution and autoscaler tuning — requires runbook and could take several hours.

Recommendation: start Option A canary now, prepare Option B as a fallback if A doesn’t hit target. I’ll queue the canary-config.diff patch for the batch-window change and prefetched key list.

One request: Marissa — if we decide to suggest quantization to the customer, we need 3 bullet points for the customer note about expected perf gains, quality caveats, and rollback plan.

—Karthik
Sr. SW Eng, Inference Runtime

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-28T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Streamline AI p95 spike — immediate tradeoffs + customer note

Thanks — I agree with the two-step approach. Some product context to weigh the tradeoff:

- Streamline routes ~18% of traffic as long-prompt generation; their evaluation set is sensitive to hallucination for rare tokens. My concern with int8 is edge-case token fidelity. We should not recommend it unless we have a quick, targeted eval showing <1% metric delta on Streamline’s critical eval.
- Enabling batch-window increase + kv-prefetch is the least risky immediate ask and buys us time.

Customer messaging guidance: keep it transparent and actionable. If we go with Option A only, propose this short draft to the customer: 
"We’re seeing a temporary increase in 95th percentile latency for long-run prompts. We’ve initiated a canary mitigation that increases short-term batching and pre-warms cache for your heaviest keys. We expect measurable improvements within 30–45 minutes and will follow up with a plan to further reduce tails."

If we include Option B (quantization) as a potential fallback, add: 
"As a fallback we may route some traffic to a low-precision variant that reduces latency further; we’ll only do this after internal validation and with an immediate rollback plan if you see any quality difference."

Jordan — please hold off on sending the attached note until we confirm canary results. Also, can you coordinate a 10–15m customer checkpoint call if the canary doesn’t quickly improve p95?

Marissa
Product Manager, Serving Platform

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: sara@streamline.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-28T09:55:22-07:00
Subject: [Draft] Quick update on latency for Streamline — action taken and next steps

Sara —

We wanted to promptly update you: starting at ~09:00 PT we observed a rise in 95th percentile latency on long-prompt generation for your account. We’ve started a targeted mitigation (canary) that does two things: (1) slightly increases internal batching for the Streamline route and (2) pre-warms the KV cache for the heaviest keys we’re seeing. The canary is running now on a single shard.

What to expect:
- We expect to see measurable p95 improvement in 30–45 minutes if the canary succeeds.
- If the canary does not bring p95 down sufficiently, our fallback is to briefly route a portion of traffic to a lower-precision serving variant (this provides further latency reduction but we will only use it after internal validation and with immediate rollback).

We do not see an increase in error rates and there is no action required from Streamline at this time. If you can avoid submitting extremely long prompts for the next hour it will help reduce tail exposure while we stabilize.

We’ll follow up with results and any next steps by 10:30 PT. Attaching a short draft with the metrics and our rollback plan for your records.

Best,
Olga Petrov
SRE Lead — Redwood Inference
